Report_ID: Stone-free rate after 3 mo (CT-assessed treatment success)
Title: Effectiveness of Flexible Ureterorenoscopy Versus Extracorporeal Shock Wave Lithotripsy for Renal Calculi of 5-15 mm: Results of a Randomized Controlled Trial
Author: Fankhauser
Comment: Success defined as fully stone free on abdominal CT at 3 mo (trial's own definition; no residual-fragment size threshold applied). Event counts and ITT denominators taken verbatim from Table 2; p = 0.55 from Fisher's exact/chi-square as stated in Methods. No risk ratio, odds ratio or confidence interval was reported by the paper, so those fields are left empty. Trial was terminated prematurely for poor accrual (44 of 214 planned patients) and is underpowered.
Participant type: Adults (18-99 yr) with newly diagnosed renal calculi 5-15 mm
Recruitment source: Tertiary care academic centre (University Hospital Zurich) outpatient/urology clinic
Outcome measurement: Number of participants fully stone free on abdominal CT at 3 mo, out of the number randomised to each arm (ITT denominators: URS 23, SWL 21)
Outcome variable: Stone-free rate after 3 mo (CT-assessed treatment success)
outcome_family: treatment success (stone-free rate) at three months

Title: A Prospective Randomized Comparison Between Shock Wave Lithotripsy and Flexible Ureterorenoscopy for Lower Caliceal Stones ≤2 cm: A Single-Center Experience
Author: Kumar, Anup; Vasudeva, Pawan; Nanda, Biswajit; Kumar, Niraj; Das, Manoj Kumar; Jha, Sanjeev Kumar
Comment: Denominators used are the numbers ANALYSED (90 per arm), as the paper reports events only for analysed patients; numbers randomised were 97 (SWL) and 98 (RIRS), so a strict ITT denominator is not reconstructable from reported data. Paper's subgroup percentages are internally inconsistent with their own counts (e.g. 45/55 reported as 84.9%, 29/35 as 78.4%), but the overall 74/90 and 78/90 counts match the stated 82.2% and 86.6%. No risk ratio or confidence interval is reported by the paper; p-value from chi-square test.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Group A – shock wave lithotripsy (SWL), outpatient, Dornier Compact Delta, up to 3000 shocks/session, max 4 sessions') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: adults (age 15–60 years) with a single radiopaque lower caliceal calculus ≤2 cm
Recruitment source: Urology Outpatient Department, single tertiary centre (Vardhman Mahaveer Medical College and Safdarjang Hospital, New Delhi)
Outcome measurement: Number of patients stone-free at 3 months out of patients analysed per arm (KUB X-ray and ultrasonography)
additional_group_ns: Randomised: Group A n=97, Group B n=98; 15 lost to follow-up (7 SWL, 8 RIRS), leaving 90 analysed per arm. Subgroups: A1 <1 cm n=55 (45 stone-free), A2 1–2 cm n=35 (29 stone-free), B1 <1 cm n=51 (43 stone-free), B2 1–2 cm n=39 (35 stone-free).
outcome_family: treatment success (stone-free rate) at three months
effect_direction: slightly favours RIRS (SWL 74/90 = 82.2% vs RIRS 78/90 = 86.6%; RR just below 1)
